record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Reverse direction of the perfectoid transfer theorem for decidability
record.original_question: Let p be a prime. The perfectoid transfer theorem of Kartas (2024) provides implications from decidability in positive characteristic to decidability in mixed characteristic: (a) if F_p((t))^{1/p^infty} (the perfect hull of F_p((t)), with t-adic valuation) has a decidable elementary or existential L_val(t)-theory, then Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}) and Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}) have decidable elementary or existential L_val-theories respectively; (b) if F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^infty} has a decidable elementary or existential L_val(t)-theory, then Q_p^{ab} has a decidable elementary or existential L_val-theory. (Here L_val is the language of valued rings and L_val(t) adds a constant for t.) It is also known (from the tilt correspondence) that decidability in L_val transfers from perfectoid fields to their tilts, giving partial converses. The precise open question is: can the argument be improved to obtain decidability in L_val(t) on the positive characteristic side, given decidability in L_val on the mixed characteristic side? That is, if Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}) or Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}) has a decidable L_val-theory, does F_p((t))^{1/p^infty} have a decidable L_val(t)-theory (not merely L_val)? And if Q_p^{ab} has a decidable L_val-theory, does F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^infty} have a decidable L_val(t)-theory?

evidence.quote: Open problem 4: What about the reverse direction? In fact, if Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}) or Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}) has a decidable L_val-theory, then F_p((t))^{1/p^infty} has a decidable L_val-theory, and if Q_p^{ab} has a decidable L_val-theory, then so does F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^infty}. ... So a more precise version of problem 4 is whether this argument can be improved to get decidability in L_val(t) on the positive characteristic side.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let p be a prime. Let L_val denote the first-order language of valued rings, and let L_val(t) denote the expansion of L_val by a single constant symbol t. Consider the following valued fields:

- F_p((t))^{1/p^∞}, the perfect hull of the Laurent series field F_p((t)), equipped with the t-adic valuation; the constant t in L_val(t) is interpreted as the uniformizer.
- F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^∞}, the perfect hull of F_p^{ac}((t)) where F_p^{ac} is an algebraic closure of F_p, again with the t-adic valuation.
- Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}), the field obtained from Q_p by adjoining all p-power roots of unity, with its unique extension of the p-adic valuation.
- Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}), the field obtained by adjoining all p-power roots of p to Q_p, with its unique extension of the p-adic valuation.
- Q_p^{ab}, the maximal abelian extension of Q_p, with its unique extension of the p-adic valuation.

It is known that decidability of the L_val-theory transfers from each of these mixed-characteristic perfectoid fields to its positive-characteristic tilt (so that L_val-decidability of Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}) or Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}) implies L_val-decidability of F_p((t))^{1/p^∞}, and L_val-decidability of Q_p^{ab} implies L_val-decidability of F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^∞}).

Question: Can this transfer be strengthened to the language L_val(t) with a named uniformizer? Specifically:

(i) If Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}) has a decidable L_val-theory, does F_p((t))^{1/p^∞} have a decidable L_val(t)-theory? Likewise, if Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}) has a decidable L_val-theory, does F_p((t))^{1/p^∞} have a decidable L_val(t)-theory?

(ii) If Q_p^{ab} has a decidable L_val-theory, does F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^∞} have a decidable L_val(t)-theory?

The analogous questions for existential theories are also asked.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a December 2025 survey on the model theory of tame valued fields, building on Kartas's perfectoid transfer theorem (2024). No resolution has been located; the converse with a named uniformizer t appears to remain open.
